mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs, reducing corporate investments and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances following RSAFS growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month indicates supply chain disruptions or reduced manufacturing activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 50% of instances following a 1% decline in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: When Housing Starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in a month, it signals a strong demand for housing, which boosts related sectors and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances following a 5% increase in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure that leads to tighter monetary policy, reducing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances following a PAYEMS increase > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: When Real GDP (GDPC1) and Real Final Sales (RSAFS) both show growth in the same quarter, it indicates robust economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both increase in the same quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 50% of instances when both GDPC1 and RSAFS increase.
